newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Nemtsov seeks Yeltsin signature for reform decrees.
newsitem.headline: Nemtsov seeks Yeltsin signature for reform decrees.

text.p: First Deputy Prime Minister Boris Nemtsov planned to present President Boris Yeltsin on Wednesday with draft decrees outlining new liberal economic reforms, Russian news agencies said.

Nemtsov left for the Volzhsky Utyos resort in central Russia, where Yeltsin is on holiday, with some of his allies in the government and hoped the president would sign the draft decrees, Itar-Tass news agency said
One decree, which the government says is vital for collecting enough cash to pay off a huge backlog of wage arrears, would allow national power utility UES to issue convertible bonds.
"Boris Nemtsov will present to the head of state draft decrees (including) the issue of bonds by RAO UES," Tass said.
Convertible bonds are bonds which can be converted into another financial instrument, sometimes another type of bond but more often into company shares.
Russian news agencies said the decree on the bonds, which are expected to hit international markets this autumn, would raise five trillion roubles ($870 million).

Nemtsov, liberal governor of Nizhny Novgorod region until he joined the government in March, was accompanied by two officials he has appointed to top state posts -- Deputy Fuel and Energy Minister Sergei Kiriyenko and UES chairman Boris Brevnov.

He also took with him a draft decree covering new rules for exporting gold. Tass quoted Nemtsov as saying the document was aimed at attracting foreign investment into gold production but gave no details.

While Nemtsov's liberal partner in the government, First Deputy Prime Minister Anatoly Chubais, is on holiday, Nemtsov is using regular visits to the president to get his backing for documents needed to continue reforms.
Central Bank Chairman Sergei Dubinin was also among the group visiting Yeltsin.

Tass said Dubinin and Yeltsin would discuss measures to strengthen the rouble but would not touch on a scandal unleashed by Dubinin accusing a bank last week of misappropriating more than $500 million in state funds.
